reading: Lisbon's Museu da Marioneta is devoted to puppet theatre: its history, techniques, preservation and living performance, with particular attention to Portuguese practice alongside traditions from around the world. It treats puppets as carriers of myths, legends and shared stories, and as things made, manipulated, studied and repaired. Its vocabulary runs from fios (strings), luva (glove) and sombras (shadows) to cenários, adereços, teatros portáteis, oficinas, conservação and restauro. Its character comes from the meeting of a collection and research library with active theatre and hands-on workshops, inside the historic Convento das Bernardas. The crawl moves between the chapel stage, storage, the Madragoa neighbourhood, colour and light experiments, mechanical puppets and a single giant figure containing many stories.

enemies.idea: The Over-Restorer stitches every moving joint rigid, then chases any puppet that still improvises as a damaged object.
enemies.why: Saving a captured ally means loosening the right stitches without pulling apart its fragile body.

enemies.idea: A portable theatre folds around a crew member, swapping its little scenery panels until the trapped person plays the part assigned by the swarm.
enemies.why: The others can intervene from outside by rearranging props in the tiny stage.

enemies.idea: The Donations Collector offers a safe home for any treasured object, then tags its owner as an accessory to be stored alongside it.
enemies.why: A tempting bargain becomes a rescue puzzle with a clear paper trail.

enemies.idea: A face-making machine reads a raised eyebrow as a command and fastens a matching expression onto everyone nearby, regardless of how they feel.
enemies.why: The crew can confuse it by acting one emotion while making another face.

enemies.idea: A colour-shadow hunter shines overlapping lamps to detach coloured silhouettes from their owners; each silhouette moves only in its own light.
enemies.why: Changing light colours divides or reunites the hunter's moving pieces.

enemies.idea: The Glove Usurper crawls over a hand and makes its wearer perform a puppet's gestures, using applause to pull the arm farther into its sleeve.
enemies.why: A partner can interrupt the rhythm or offer it a decoy hand.

enemies.idea: A sponge puppet absorbs sounds until the room falls silent, then squeezes out the stolen noises as misleading footsteps and calls.
enemies.why: Its squishy body is both cover and a reservoir of clues.

enemies.idea: The movement-logic automaton predicts the next pose in a repeated action and winds a string around the joint before it arrives.
enemies.why: Breaking a rhythm or improvising an awkward movement defeats its prediction.

enemies.idea: A workshop-built automaton walks a perfect circuit, harvesting loose puppet parts to repair itself whenever its crank completes a turn.
enemies.why: The exposed crank offers a timing challenge and its scavenged parts can be recovered.

enemies.idea: The Point-of-View dragon is invisible from its flat side and enormous from its painted front, rotating scenery to keep its prey in the wrong position.
enemies.why: The crew must coordinate from different viewing angles to find its narrow profile.

enemies.idea: A treasure-hunt marionette lays a trail of enticing clues that circle back to its waiting direct-manipulation hands.
enemies.why: The clues are solvable, but reading their physical trail reveals the trap.

enemies.idea: The Thread-Router stretches strings along the puppet routes between European cities, pulling distant puppets into one marching formation.
enemies.why: Cutting one line changes the formation while leaving other routes live.

enemies.idea: Bottle-to-puppet scavengers collect discarded bottles as bodies, swapping heads and limbs whenever one gets stuck in a narrow passage.
enemies.why: Their modular bodies make obstacles and loose parts useful to both sides.

enemies.idea: A zoetrope patrol advances only while its slits spin; when stopped, it breaks into still poses that can be rearranged before motion resumes.
enemies.why: A crew can turn a chase into a tactile animation puzzle.

enemies.idea: Suspended mythology mobiles cast a net of counterweighted figures; removing one makes the others dip and reach for the thief.
enemies.why: The crew can balance the mobile with substitute weights instead of fighting every figure.

enemies.idea: A mechanical candle-blower turns every extinguished birthday candle into one more crank powering its grasping arms.
enemies.why: Relighting candles steals its power, but reveals the crew's position.

enemies.idea: The Catalogue Keeper classifies moving visitors as collection objects and sends numbered puppet hands to put them in their allotted places.
enemies.why: Swapping number tags lets the crew redirect the hands and free a captive.

enemies.idea: A paper-theatre precision cutter folds scenery into tiny exact replicas of the room, then cuts the miniature to open corresponding gaps in its stage machinery.
enemies.why: Protecting or altering the model changes the terrain the crew must cross.

enemies.idea: The Chapel Chorus forces every puppet company into the same performance, using a conductor's strings to silence any performer who changes the scene.
enemies.why: An improvised counter-performance can tangle the conductor's cues.

enemies.idea: A story-gathering marionette steals the endings of local legends, leaving characters to repeat their beginnings until it can add them to its own script.
enemies.why: Giving a character a new ending releases it and changes the encounter.

enemies.idea: The Last-Entry Usher stamps anything moving after 17:30 as a late arrival and escorts it into a portable waiting room.
enemies.why: Its rigid schedule creates a predictable window for sneaking past or rescuing someone.

enemies.idea: A shadow-theatre machinist cuts new silhouettes from the crew's cast shadows and sends them across walls to operate distant switches.
enemies.why: Moving the light can stretch, shrink or separate the copies from their controls.

allies.idea: A careful restoration puppet can splint a damaged ally without taking away its ability to move, if the crew brings back its scattered tools.
allies.why: It turns the museum's care for objects into a practical reason to explore.

allies.idea: An educational workshop puppet teaches the crew to make a simple shadow double that can distract swarm sensors for one scene.
allies.why: A hands-on lesson becomes a reusable trick learned through play.

allies.idea: A cat and mouse stage pair have kept their unlikely friendship despite the swarm; one slips through gaps while the other distracts guards.
allies.why: Their different sizes make cooperation useful in a small rescue.

allies.idea: A listening puppet carries fragments of performers' voices between safe rooms and can find a route to a person by following their story.
allies.why: The museum's effort to keep listening becomes a network for locating allies.

bosses.idea: The Thousand-Story Figure is a gigantic flat puppet assembled from many narrative worlds. The swarm tries to make every story end identically; the crew can free individual panels and let their characters pull in different directions.
bosses.why: A single enormous figure becomes a multi-stage fight about restoring many voices.

bosses.idea: The Grand Conservator has fused storage racks, portable stages and puppet strings into a walking theatre. It preserves every performance by forcing it to repeat forever; each freed stage changes the machine's movement.
bosses.why: The museum's collection and living theatre combine into a boss that can be dismantled through performance and rescue.

bosses.idea: The Chapel's Master of Cues controls a company of mismatched puppets from a web of strings above the stage. Each borrowed technique gives it a different phase, until the crew persuades the performers to improvise together.
bosses.why: The whole performance space becomes an ensemble encounter with an alternative to simply cutting everything down.

events.idea: A shadow puppet begs the crew to find its missing coloured light before its silhouette fades into the others on a wall.
events.why: A quick light-positioning puzzle can earn a guide through the next room.

events.idea: A portable theatre in storage is playing a rescue scene that exactly mirrors a locked cabinet nearby; changing a prop in the play opens the cabinet.
events.why: Watching the miniature performance supplies a concrete clue.

events.idea: Two workshop puppets argue over whether a smile or a frown belongs on a recovered face; both expressions are needed to signal different doors.
events.why: The crew can resolve the argument by trying expressions rather than guessing a single answer.

events.idea: A trail of sardine-shaped puppets crosses the cloister, each carrying a piece of a map back to the neighbourhood.
events.why: Following the procession offers a gentle chase and a useful route.

events.idea: A bottle puppet is missing its cap and keeps leaking the tiny beads it uses as footsteps; return the cap or follow the beads to its stranded companions.
events.why: The same small problem supplies both a rescue and a trail.

events.idea: A zoetrope has a single frame out of order, trapping a little puppet in a repeated fall. Rearrange the frames while the drum is still.
events.why: A visible animation loop makes the solution easy to experiment with.

events.idea: The crew finds a mobile of suspended myths tilted over a safe passage; replacing one missing weight opens the route without cutting any strings.
events.why: Every object carried by the crew becomes a possible counterweight.

events.idea: A birthday crank powers a locked door, but each turn blows out a candle. Keep one candle lit while a partner winds the mechanism.
events.why: A simple cooperative timing challenge grows out of the workshop's candles and cranks.

events.idea: A puppet-led walk from the museum toward Madragoa has lost its guide's strings at a fork. Reconnect them to reveal which direction the guide remembers.
events.why: The crew physically repairs a route instead of reading a map.

events.idea: An unfinished glove puppet offers to help open a latch, but needs a hand inside it; the volunteer must coordinate with a partner who can see the latch.
events.why: Manipulation becomes a small trust and communication challenge.

events.idea: A locked documentation room contains a puppet trying to recall a lost manipulation technique. Bring it a working example and it will demonstrate a way past a string trap.
events.why: Research and practical craft reward each other.

events.idea: The chapel's performers are stuck waiting for a cue that will never come. Give them an improvised opening and their performance draws a patrol away.
events.why: A performance becomes a diversion the crew creates with the ensemble.

events.idea: A cat puppet is trying to teach a bird-shaped prop to fly across a gap; adjusting its strings makes a bridge for a small messenger.
events.why: A visual theatre exercise becomes a traversal solution.

events.idea: A collection of optical objects projects a different route across the floor from each angle. Two crew members must compare what they see to find the safe path.
events.why: Different viewpoints give each player useful information.
